children: Zero Federal Reserve officials currently foresee downside risks to U.S. GDP growth, in a historic display of economic confidence.

This marks the first time since the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee began publishing its Summary of Economic Projections that no members reported downside risks to GDP growth, Charles Schwab strategist Kevin Gordon wrote in a recent social media post.

to the Federal Reserve's long-term outlook: the FOMC's median real GDP growth projection for 2026 has been raised to +2.3%, up from June's estimate of +2.2%. Expectations for 2027 also ticked up to +2.4% from +2.3%, while the 2028 forecast remains steady at +2.2%.

This long-term optimism is mirrored by booming near-term data, with the Atlanta Fed’s Q3 real GDP tracker jumped to +5.1% as of Thursday. This represents the highest reading since Aug. 6 and marks a significant increase from +4.42% just six days prior, sitting well above the blue-chip consensus of around +2.5%, according to market strategist Neil Sethi.
The recent surge was mainly driven by a stronger contribution from consumption—rising from +2.43% to +2.83% following a robust
report—alongside a minor increase in government spending.
However, Sethi cautioned that Atlanta Fed trackers for Q1 and Q2 were similarly strong before falling sharply ahead of the actual GDP prints.

Meanwhile, on prediction marketplace Kalshi, the odds of the economy "overheating"—defined as unemployment remaining below 5% while inflation sits at or above 3.5%—have spiked to 72.4%, far eclipsing the 32% chance traders assign to a traditional soft landing.

title: Fed officials unanimously ditch downside GDP risks for first time
